claims.conditions: A written plan whose tasks are largely independent, a harness with a subagent dispatch tool that accepts an explicit model choice, an isolated worktree, and the skill's bundled scripts, prompt templates and reference files installed. No pending step falls into the source's four stop categories. Invocation must already be permitted by the user, the harness and applicable policy; this claim describes suitability under the stated conditions and grants no permission to invoke.
claims.rationale: The controller dispatches a fresh implementer per task and a task review after each, with the instruction 'Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping' (line 17) and 'A running plan does not wait on a human' (line 19). Structure bounds the autonomy: implementers are never dispatched in parallel (line 235), a task review covering both spec compliance and quality is mandatory (line 256), the controller may not move on with open Critical or Important issues (line 317), the fix loop has a round cap held in a reference file (line 302), and a ledger file is the recovery record across compaction (lines 108-126). Plausible failure modes: much of the procedure lives in reference files, prompts and scripts outside the inspected file, so the loop cannot run as written if they are absent; every task costs several subagent dispatches; a wrong controller ruling propagates through later tasks; harnesses without a per-dispatch model parameter cannot satisfy line 160. Falsified if controllers skip the per-task review or advance past open Critical findings.
